# RSA and JWT fixture provenance

`conformance/rsa-wycheproof.json` retains all 259 cases from `testvectors_v1/rsa_signature_2048_sha256_test.json` in [C2SP/Wycheproof](https://github.com/C2SP/wycheproof/blob/3fa63dd0344abb611f1fb1d77e119938603ea230/testvectors_v1/rsa_signature_2048_sha256_test.json), retrieved September 14, 2026. Only repository-formatter whitespace differs. SHA-256 of the upstream bytes: `94a917b01ff50fb874cfc05bf29b4af44868d944a6558201cf18380da93fb393`; formatted file: `aa8e27ed74fc23109fc4c392c50bd4f0cfdab8d7906757c94df4b71e07ad0130`. The source is [Apache-2.0 licensed](https://github.com/C2SP/wycheproof/blob/3fa63dd0344abb611f1fb1d77e119938603ea230/LICENSE). All nine valid cases must verify; all 249 invalid cases must reject. The one upstream “acceptable” MissingNull case must reject under our strict DER profile. No vectors were generated with Theoria or Noble.

`conformance/rsa-openssl.json` contains four independently generated keys: 2048/e=3, 2049/e=3, 3072/e=65537, and 4096/e=4294967295. Each key signs empty, asymmetric binary, and 8192-byte messages. OpenSSL verifies all 12 genuine signatures and rejects all 24 recorded altered-message/altered-signature pairs before the generator retains them. Actual key sizes and exponents are checked against OpenSSL's public-key output; requesting an odd key size alone is insufficient because some OpenSSL generation paths round it down. Exponent 3 uses the default provider, not the FIPS provider. Theoria and Noble are not used to produce expected cryptographic results.

Regenerate with `bun run packages/sign/scripts/generate-rsa-fixtures.ts`, then format the JSON with the repository's Prettier and review/update its hash in `conformance/sources.manifest.json`. Regeneration creates new keys and signatures; private keys are removed by Effect's scoped temporary-directory finalizer. The retained fixture records the OpenSSL version and contains no private key material.

`bun run --filter @scenesystems/sign fixtures:check` verifies the RSA and JWT payload schemas and their SHA-256 fingerprints alongside the existing conformance payloads. CI runs that same command. These checks establish fixture integrity and conformance evidence, not an independent cryptographic audit.

`conformance/jwt-openssl.json` and `conformance/jwt-access-openssl.json` are generated by `bun run packages/sign/scripts/generate-jwt-fixtures.ts`. Each corpus has a separate ephemeral 2048-bit RSA key (exponent 65537), and its `generator` field records the OpenSSL version. OpenSSL signs each exact protected input with `openssl dgst -sha256 -sign`, exports the public key, and successfully verifies every signature with `openssl dgst -sha256 -verify` before either fixture is retained. The Effect Platform program scopes its temporary directories and deletes both private keys on completion. Only public JWKs and signed examples are retained; Theoria's production signer and runtime WebCrypto signing are not used. Regeneration creates new keys and signatures. The current SHA-256 values are `70faa3538831048eddd3631bc3f9044b5d6b1f44e84f7502b85fbce9506c76c2` for `jwt-openssl.json` and `c045783ddd618d68be59ef90352f20fe92bb8ecc20f1d7dd6b5b6a7918099798` for `jwt-access-openssl.json`.

Policy expectations are specified independently in the generator: issuer `https://team.example`, audience `app`, maximum lifetime 3600 seconds, verification time 150 seconds after Unix epoch, required nonempty subject, and email `reader@example.test`. JSON whitespace, array audiences, duplicate-member semantics, strict UTF-8, claim failures, and unsupported protected-header parameters are intentionally represented. These fixtures contain only synthetic test identities.

The Access corpus freezes this Worker-consumable profile: issuer `https://team.example`; audience `app`; maximum lifetime 86400 seconds (24 hours); verification time 150 seconds after Unix epoch (set `TestClock` to 150000 milliseconds); required nonempty `sub`; and required `email` in the allow-list containing only `reader@example.test`. `iat` and present `nbf` are inclusive at the known time, `exp` is exclusive, and absent `nbf` is accepted. Its 27 expected outcomes comprise six valid tokens, sixteen `Claims` rejections, and five `MalformedToken` rejections. Missing, empty, and denied identity claims; wrong issuer/audience; missing and malformed times; all time boundaries; maximum/excess lifetime; audience arrays; optional `nbf`; algorithm confusion; protected-header excess; malformed JSON/UTF-8; and BOM handling are signed cases. Key-set variations reuse the first valid signed token: missing, wrong-`kid`, or duplicate matches reject as `KeySelection`; a matching JWK with `use: "enc"` rejects as `InvalidKey`.

## One-off weakening experiment, 2026-09-14

Each change below was applied separately and tested with `bunx vitest run packages/sign/test/rsa.test.ts` or `packages/sign/test/jwt.test.ts`. Every run exited 1 because of a behavioral failure. Both production files were restored byte-for-byte, and the unchanged 10-test RSA/JWT baseline passed afterward. No mutation framework, test of test structure, or permanent weakening was retained.

| Deliberately weakened control                                              | Existing behavior that failed                                        |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| RSA modulus-width signature check                                          | Wrong-width signature accepted instead of `InvalidVerificationInput` |
| RSA representative less than modulus                                       | Wycheproof case 244 accepted; range-boundary test also failed        |
| Entire recovered encoding compared; replaced with digest-suffix comparison | Wycheproof case 8 (MissingNull) accepted                             |
| JWT RS256 algorithm restriction                                            | Independently signed algorithm-confusion fixture accepted            |
| JWT unique matching key; replaced with first match                         | Duplicate-key rejection failed                                       |
| JWT verification result required                                           | Tampered token reached application policy                            |
| JWT issuer equality                                                        | Wrong-issuer fixture accepted                                        |
| JWT audience membership                                                    | Wrong-audience fixture accepted                                      |
| JWT exclusive expiry; changed to inclusive                                 | Expiry-equals-now fixture and execution-time boundary failed         |

## Small Bun baseline, 2026-09-14

Run `bun run --filter @scenesystems/sign benchmark:rsa` separately from builds/tests. Each case has 100 warmups and 1000 sequential observations. The p50/p95 values use exact nearest ranks (500 and 950). `Effect.timedWith` reads live monotonic time through `TestServices.provideLive`; only JWT claim time is fixed with `TestClock`. Throughput includes measurement and verdict-check overhead. Every iteration must return the expected genuine/nonmatch result; unrelated failures stop the benchmark.

Observed in a Linux x64 orb on Bun 1.3.9, Effect 3.22.1, Noble curves/hashes 2.4.0:

| Public API workload                         | p50 ms | p95 ms | Operations/s |
| ------------------------------------------- | -----: | -----: | -----------: |
| RSA 2048/e=65537, genuine                   |  0.606 |  1.015 |         1375 |
| RSA 2048/e=65537, nonmatch                  |  0.568 |  0.862 |         1510 |
| RSA 4096/e=4294967295, 8192 bytes, genuine  |  7.037 | 12.040 |          125 |
| RSA 4096/e=4294967295, 8192 bytes, nonmatch |  6.874 | 11.508 |          128 |
| JWT 2048/e=65537, genuine                   |  0.892 |  1.180 |         1002 |
| JWT 2048/e=65537, nonmatch                  |  0.832 |  1.073 |         1067 |

RSA includes validation, copying, hashing, arithmetic, and comparison, with an already imported key. JWT includes parsing, JWK import, verification, and claim policy. Fixture loading and construction of the reusable Effects are outside timing. This is a warm, single-process baseline, not an SLA, load test, cold-start profile, or Workers measurement. In particular, worst-admitted RSA is materially more expensive than ordinary verification; synchronous arithmetic is not preempted by an Effect timeout.
